The House GOP's push for Medicaid guardrails is about fiscal sanity, not cruelty. The real issue? Bureaucrats have let the program balloon into a $800B/year behemoth with minimal accountability. Work requirements for able-bodied adults mirror the 2018 Arkansas model that saw employment rates jump 12% without mass coverage losses.

Blocking payments to ineligible groups isn't radical—it's basic stewardship when improper payments hit $80B+ annually. The proposed per capita caps (House Budget Committee's FY2025 plan, Section 3A) force states to prioritize truly vulnerable populations over expansion enrollees.

Opponents screaming "draconian cuts" ignore that Medicaid spending still grows 5% annually under these reforms—just not at the unsustainable 9% rate of unchecked bureaucracy. Protect the safety net by tightening it, not stretching it beyond recognition.
